summary: Candy executive Robert Welch founded the John Birch Society in 1958, building a secretive anti-communist network that branded Eisenhower a Soviet agent, fought civil rights and powered Barry Goldwater's 1964 campaign.

evidence.note: Welch's birth in North Carolina in 1899 and child-prodigy schooling
John Birch's missionary and wartime years in China, long segment
Birch killed by Communist soldiers in 1945 after Japan's surrender
December 1958 Indianapolis meeting founds the society
campaign to impeach Earl Warren over Brown v. Board; civil rights framed as communist plot
leak of The Politician calling Eisenhower a conscious communist agent
society builds early right-wing media network: radio, magazines, reading rooms
society's volunteer machine secures Goldwater's 1964 nomination
legacy segment: society still active, influence on Tea Party and Trump era

notes: Title names the society, but the story is equally a biography of Welch, so both are primary and the lifetime rule sets covered_span to 1899-1985. Main span runs from the 1958 founding to the 1967 decline. Legacy through the Tea Party and 2020 sets reaches_present. China earns a setting slot for the John Birch segment.
